title: Annotatio V §.XII close: Sennertus §.LXV same of Coena — stop before Annotatio VI Indignorum
pass_a_gloss: And with a few things inserted Sennertus continues: (8) Further they are necessary to salvation in a qualified sense, as said above, by reason of divine mandate, insofar as God from abundance willed to fortify our faith with certain signs and seals … which (9) in a case of necessity we can indeed lack without loss of faith and eternal salvation. At last, that what was said of Sacraments in general may also apply to the sacrament of the Supper, §. LXV. he thus concludes: What was said of Sacraments in genus or common, let the same judgment be of each in species of both O. and N. Testament — Circumcision, the Paschal Lamb, Baptism, and the HOLY SUPPER.
pass_b_english: Sennert continues: they are necessary to salvation only in a qualified sense (God’s abundant seals); in necessity we may lack them without losing faith or eternal salvation.
§.LXV: what holds of sacraments in general holds of each — circumcision, Passover lamb, baptism, and the Holy Supper. Stop §.XII before Annotatio VI (Indignorum).
source_text: Et paucis intersertis pergit Sennertus: (8) Necessaria porrò adeo, sunt ad salutem secundum quid, ut suprà dictum, ratione mandati divini, quatenus ex abundanti DEUS fidem nostram munire signis & sigillis certis voluit … quibus (9) in casu necessitatis carere quidem possumus extrà jacturam fidei & salutis æternæ. Tandem, quò dicta de Sacramentis in genere, etiam Sacramento cœnæ applicentur, §. LXV. ita concludit: Quod de Sacramentis in genere vel communi dictum, idem esto judicium de singulis in specie & V. & N. Testamenti, Circumcisione, Agno Paschali, Baptismo & S. CŒNA.
